key_insight: SymPlex discovers analytic symbolic solutions to PDEs without ground-truth formulas by casting expression generation as tree-structured decision-making and using a structure-aware Transformer (SymFormer) that captures hierarchical symbolic dependencies and enforces syntactic validity.
problem_solved: Current symbolic PDE solvers either require supervised examples or fail to model the hierarchical, syntactic structure of analytic expressions; SymPlex finds interpretable closed-form solutions using only the PDE and its boundary conditions.
method: Formulate symbolic PDE solving as a tree-structured reinforcement learning problem where candidate expression trees are generated and scored by PDE residuals and boundary-condition satisfaction.
Introduce SymFormer, a structure-aware Transformer with tree-relative self-attention and syntax constraints to model hierarchical token dependencies and ensure syntactically valid expressions.
Iterative search/optimization loop that refines candidate analytic expressions using only the PDE + boundary conditions as reward signals (no ground-truth expressions needed).
impact: Enables data-free discovery of interpretable analytic PDE solutions, reducing reliance on labeled symbolic datasets and accelerating scientific modeling, verification, and compact surrogate creation for ML-driven engineering.
visual_elements: RL feedback loop diagram: PDE + boundary conditions → generator (tree actions) → candidate symbolic expression → PDE residual & BC reward → policy update
SymFormer architecture sketch highlighting tree-relative self-attention and syntactic masking over an expression tree
Before/after comparison: numeric PDE solution vs discovered analytic solution (plots and residual heatmap)
Expression-tree visualization showing tokens, hierarchical structure, and enforced syntax (valid/invalid examples)
paper_title: SymPlex: A Structure-Aware Transformer for Symbolic PDE Solving
paper_authors: Yesom Park, Annie C. Lu, Shao-Ching Huang, Qiyang Hu, Y. Sungtaek Ju
